chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), regarding

a man who blinded the eyes of a man and cut off his ears, then killed him. He (peace be upon him) said: If he separated between those (injuries), he would be retaliated for them, then he would be killed. And if he struck him with one strike, his neck would be struck, and he would not be retaliated for them.

key_terms.فَرَّقَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ: He separated between that (injuries at different times)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in qisas (retaliation) when multiple injuries are inflicted at different times versus a single strike?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between cumulative and simultaneous injuries in the law of qisas, emphasizing that the timing of the blows determines whether individual compensations are aggregated or subsumed by the capital punishment. It reflects the Shia scholarly focus on precise legal causality, where separate acts of aggression incur separate retributions, while a single decisive strike leading to death precludes additional bodily retaliation. This principle ensures proportional justice by distinguishing between distinct legal violations and a singular fatal act.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 5<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) regarding

a man who blinded an eye of a man and cut-off his ear, then killed him. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If there was a separation between that (different times), he would be retaliated from, then he would be killed. And if he had struck him with one strike, his neck would be struck, and he would not be retaliated from’.
